approach: skyline bottom-left fill with rotations and reflections
details: Input: read n, then for each piece i read k_i followed by k_i (x,y) lines. Precompute the 8 orientations per piece (rotations 0,1,2,3 combined with reflection 0,1); for each orientation translate so min cell is (0,0) and store cells as a vector of (dx,dy). For each orientation cache bbox width w, bbox height h, and an array min_dy_at_col[dx] over occupied columns plus the max dy at each column. Let T be the total cell count and start W at ceil(sqrt(T)). Sort original piece indices by their largest orientation bbox area descending (tiebreak: k_i descending). For each candidate W, maintain skyline[0..W-1] initialized to zero and a W by W occupancy bitset. For each piece in sorted order, scan every orientation and every x0 in 0..W-w; compute drop y0 = max over occupied columns dx of (skyline[x0+dx] - min_dy_at_col[dx]); if y0 + h is greater than W skip; verify with the occupancy bitset that no cell collides (concave shapes may need an upper-row cell to clear a lower lip); score lex by (y0 + h, y0, x0) ascending and keep the best (orientation, x0, y0). If no placement exists at this W, increment W and restart packing from scratch. After placing, mark cells in the bitset and update skyline at each used column dx to max(skyline[x0+dx], y0 + max_dy_at_col[dx] + 1). Track per original index the chosen (X,Y,R,F): the local cell (cx,cy) maps by first applying F (when F=1 send (cx,cy) to (-cx,cy)), then R clockwise quarter rotations, then translation (X,Y); pick (X,Y) so the bottom-left of the transformed piece sits at (x0,y0). Output W W on line one followed by n lines of X Y R F in original input order.
rationale: Establishes a strong baseline that exploits the full 8-orientation symmetry and a skyline drop heuristic prioritizing large pieces; this is a fresh direction since the artifact archive was cleared for the new run.

details: Keep the orientation precomputation, piece ordering, skyline, and occupancy bitset from the current solution. Change only the placement-scoring step inside the BL search. For each candidate (orientation, x0, y0=skyline-drop), after the overlap check, compute a contact count C as the number of unit edges of the piece that touch either the rectangle boundary or an already-occupied cell. Concretely, for every piece cell (cx,cy) at (gx,gy)=(x0+cx,y0+cy), examine the 4 neighbors (gx+dx,gy+dy) for (dx,dy) in (1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1): if the neighbor lies outside [0,W)x[0,W) increment C; else if occ at that neighbor is 1 increment C; do not count neighbors that are themselves cells of the same piece being placed (build a small hash set or boolean grid of the piece-cells first to exclude them). Replace the current lexicographic score (y0+h, y0, x0) with (y0+h ascending, C descending, y0 ascending, x0 ascending). The primary key still keeps the skyline low; the C tiebreak rewards filling corners and pockets so concave shapes get plugged tightly. Skyline and occupancy updates after placement are unchanged. If no candidate exists at the current W, increment W and restart packing exactly as before. Output format unchanged (W W on first line; per-piece X Y R F in original input order).
rationale: Adds the well-known contact (touching-perimeter) heuristic as a tiebreak inside BL drop, which empirically reduces internal holes and tightens packing of concave polyominoes; continues to refine the still-young BL direction.

approach: true bottom-left with per-column bitmap collision
details: Keep input parsing, the 8-orientation precomputation (cols, min_dy, max_dy, bbox w h, min_tx, min_ty), the piece ordering by max bbox area descending then k descending, and the W=ceil(sqrt(T)) start with W increment on failure. Replace the W by W vector occ with a packed bitmap: for each global column gx an array col_bits[gx] of ceil(W/64) uint64 words where bit y of word w means row 64w+y of column gx is occupied. Replace the skyline-drop y0 with a full bitmap search so pieces can slide below the skyline into pockets under lateral overhangs. For each (piece, orientation) precompute per piece-column dx the list pattern_dx of dys where the piece has a cell. For each candidate (orientation, x0) build an aggregate blocked uint64 array total_blocked of ceil(W/64) words initialized to zero. For each piece column dx and each dy in pattern_dx, compute the rightshift-by-dy of col_bits[x0+dx] (this gives a bitset where bit y is 1 iff row y+dy of column x0+dx is occupied) and OR it into total_blocked. Also OR in an upper-tail mask that sets all bits at indices greater than or equal to (W minus h plus 1) so out-of-top y0 values are blocked. Find the lowest 0-bit of total_blocked at index 0..W-h using builtin_ctzll on the bitwise NOT of each word from low to high; that index is y0. If no such 0-bit exists, skip this (orientation, x0). Compute contact count C as before: for each piece cell at global (gx,gy)=(x0+cx,y0+cy), examine the 4 neighbors and count those that are out of bounds in 0..W or whose bit is set in col_bits[neighbor_gx], excluding neighbors that are part of the same piece being placed (use a small w by h boolean pmask of the piece-cells to exclude). Score (orientation, x0, y0) lex by (y0+h ascending, C descending, y0 ascending, x0 ascending) and keep the best. Placement update: for each piece cell (cx,cy) set bit (y0+cy) of col_bits[x0+cx]. Skyline arrays are no longer required for placement and may be removed. Per-piece (X,Y,R,F) recovery: same as current code; X = x0 - o.min_tx, Y = y0 - o.min_ty, R = orientation modulo 4, F = orientation divided by 4. Output W W on line one then n lines of X Y R F in original input order.
rationale: True BL placement lets concave pieces tuck under lateral overhangs that the skyline-only drop misses, which should reduce wasted column-space and continue the still-maturing BL direction toward a tighter pack.

details: Keep all of iter-2 structures (8 orientations per piece, true-BL placement via per-column bitmap, contact-count tiebreak, scoring tuple of y0+h asc then C desc then y0 asc then x0 asc, placement recovery via X=x0-min_tx and Y=y0-min_ty). Add a second piece-ordering used as a fallback within each W trial. Precompute two orderings of the piece indices: order1 equals the current one (maxArea desc, k desc); order2 sorts by the maximum over all 8 orientations of max(o.w, o.h) descending, tiebreak by k desc, then by maxArea desc. In the outer W loop starting at W = ceil(sqrt(T)) and incrementing by 1 on failure, for each W first run the full greedy pack using order1 into a temporary col_bits and temporary (tX,tY,tR,tF) arrays. If every piece is placed successfully, copy temporaries into outX/outY/outR/outF and break. If any piece fails to find a placement under order1, reset col_bits to all zeros (and the temporary outputs) and run the full greedy pack at the same W using order2; if order2 succeeds, copy its temporaries out and break. If both orderings fail at this W, increment W and continue. Reuse a single col_bits allocation (re-zeroed at the start of each trial) and a single set of temp arrays to keep memory flat. The per-piece BL inner search (orientation loop, bitmap shift-OR into total_blocked, ctzll-based lowest-zero search, contact-count, lexicographic best tracking) is unchanged. Output format unchanged: line one is W W; subsequent n lines are X Y R F in original input order. Edge note: order2 may produce a different placement geometry, but the temporary buffers ensure outX/outY/outR/outF only ever reflect a fully completed pack, so a failed order1 cannot corrupt the final output.
rationale: Diverse orderings often unlock a smaller W when one ordering hits a local dead-end that the other avoids, and max-dimension-first is the standard complement to max-area-first; this widens the BL search at roughly the cost of one extra packing attempt only at W values where the first ordering already fails, so it continues maturing the still-improving BL direction without changing the per-piece engine.

approach: floor-match scoring with k-descending fallback ordering
details: Keep all iter-3 structures intact (8 orientations per piece, true-BL placement via per-column bitmap col_bits, contact count C, multi-ordering fallback chain). Two changes. Change A: add a per-column top-of-stack array hh of length W; hh[gx] holds one plus the highest occupied row in column gx (0 if the column is empty); after each successful piece placement, for each piece column dx update hh[x0+dx] to max of hh[x0+dx] and y0 plus o.max_dy[dx] plus 1; reset hh to all zeros at the start of each tryPack call (alongside the col_bits reset). Change B: insert a new scoring criterion called floor_match between y0+h and C. For a candidate (orientation, x0, y0), floor_match is the count of piece columns dx for which y0 plus o.min_dy[dx] equals hh[x0+dx], that is, the bottom piece-cell at that column rests directly on the prior column-top below. Replace the scoring tuple with the lexicographic order (y0+h ascending, floor_match descending, C descending, y0 ascending, x0 ascending). Change C: extend the fallback chain in main from order1 plus order2 to order1 plus order2 plus order3, where order3 sorts piece indices by k_i descending then maxArea descending then maxDim descending (a genuinely different lead, purely cell-count-driven). The W-trial body becomes try order1; on failure try order2; on failure try order3; on failure increment W. Reuse a single col_bits and hh allocation re-zeroed at the start of each tryPack call. Edge note: a freshly empty column has hh equal to 0, so a piece resting on the rectangle floor counts as a floor-match. Output format unchanged: line one W W, then n lines X Y R F in original input order.
rationale: Floor-match directly rewards the bottom-bearing fit that BL aims for and breaks ties between equally low top-edges with a finer discriminator than total contact while a cell-count-driven third ordering widens the W-trial search to expose smaller feasible W values; continues the still-maturing BL direction.

details: Revert to c795078 (iter-3 baseline) and apply two changes. Change A: add a per-column top-of-stack array hh of length W to each tryPack call; hh[gx] is one plus the highest occupied row in column gx (0 if empty); reset hh to zero alongside col_bits at the top of tryPack; after each successful placement, for each piece column dx update hh[x0+dx] to max(hh[x0+dx], y0 + o.max_dy[dx] + 1). Change B: insert a new scoring criterion gap_sum between y0+h and C. For a candidate (orientation, x0, y0), gap_sum is the sum over dx in o.cols of max(0, y0 + o.min_dy[dx] - hh[x0+dx]); this counts the empty cells that the piece floats above the current column-tops at the piece-occupied columns (concave pockets of the piece that hang over a taller pillar contribute zero because of the clamp at 0). Replace the iter-3 scoring tuple (y0+h asc, C desc, y0 asc, x0 asc) with (y0+h ascending, gap_sum ascending, C descending, y0 ascending, x0 ascending); gap_sum is preferred lower since a placement with no floating cells is the tightest fit at the given top-edge. Keep all other iter-3 structures intact (8 orientations per piece, true-BL via per-column bitmap col_bits with shift-OR and ctzll lowest-zero search, contact count C unchanged, order1 by maxArea desc then k desc, order2 by maxDim desc then k desc then maxArea desc, fallback chain of try order1 then order2 then increment W). Do not introduce a third ordering. Reuse a single col_bits and hh allocation re-zeroed at the start of each tryPack call. Edge note: a fresh empty column has hh equal to 0, so a piece column resting on the rectangle floor contributes zero gap. Output format unchanged: line one W W, then n lines X Y R F in original input order.
rationale: Gap-sum is a finer-grained packing-tightness signal than the iter-4 floor-match (which counted only zero-gap columns), so it should discriminate better among placements that share the lowest top-edge while avoiding the regression floor-match introduced; this revives the iter-2 to iter-3 maturing trend by replacing the failed iter-4 scoring with a more informative variant.

approach: BL with K-piece lookahead candidate selection
details: Revert to c795078 (iter 3 baseline). Keep all iter-3 structures (8 orientations per piece with min_tx, min_ty, w, h, cols, min_dy, max_dy, pattern_dx; true-BL placement via per-column bitmap col_bits with shift-OR aggregation into total_blocked and ctzll lowest-zero search bounded by y0 less or equal to W minus o.h; contact-count C; per-piece recovery X=x0-min_tx, Y=y0-min_ty, R=orientation modulo 4, F=orientation divided by 4). Keep both orderings: order1 by maxArea desc then k desc, order2 by maxDim desc then k desc then maxArea desc. Keep the fallback chain in main: try order1, on failure try order2, on failure W++. Drop the iter-5 hh and gap_sum machinery entirely; the lex tuple inside the BL inner search reverts to (y0+h ascending, C descending, y0 ascending, x0 ascending). Change (new placement strategy inside tryPack): add a placed boolean array of length n initialized to false at the top of tryPack and an integer scanFront initialized to 0. Outer step loop runs until all n pieces are placed. In each step, scan order starting at scanFront and collect up to K=4 unplaced piece indices in order; advance scanFront past already-placed entries during this scan. For each collected candidate, run the full iter-3 BL inner search to compute its best lex tuple and best (orientation, x0, y0); if no valid placement exists at this W for that candidate, treat its lex tuple as positive infinity. Among the K candidate-best tuples, select the candidate with the smallest lex tuple; ties broken by the candidate that appears earliest in order. If all K candidates have infinite lex tuples, return false from tryPack (failure at this W). Otherwise place the selected candidate: write its cells into col_bits, set placed[chosen]=true, fill tF, tR, tX, tY for that piece using the recovery formulas. Continue stepping until all pieces are placed; return true. Reuse a single col_bits allocation re-zeroed at the start of each tryPack call. Output format unchanged: line one W W, then n lines X Y R F in original input order.
rationale: K-piece lookahead lets the placer pick the piece that fits the current state best at every step instead of being locked into a fixed sort order, exploring more of the placement landscape than any single ordering can; this opens a genuinely new direction since gap-sum scoring did not move iter-5 past iter-3 and the BL direction has flattened around 75.5.

approach: multi-start BL with within-tier shuffled orderings
details: Revert to c795078 (iter-3 baseline). Keep all iter-3 structures intact: 8 orientations per piece (with min_tx, min_ty, w, h, cols, min_dy, max_dy, pattern_dx, cells); true-BL placement via per-column bitmap col_bits with shift-OR aggregation into total_blocked and ctzll lowest-zero search bounded by y0 less or equal to W minus o.h; contact-count C; lex tuple (y0+h ascending, C descending, y0 ascending, x0 ascending); per-piece recovery X=x0-min_tx, Y=y0-min_ty, R=orientation mod 4, F=orientation div 4; order1 by maxArea desc then k desc; order2 by maxDim desc then k desc then maxArea desc. Add multi-start within-tier random shuffling. After computing order1 in main, build a vector tier_groups that groups order1 positions by the maxArea value of the piece at that position: walk through order1 in order and start a new group whenever maxArea changes; each group stores the contiguous range of order1 positions belonging to that maxArea tier. Add an mt19937 rng seeded with 0xC0FFEE for determinism. Add a helper makeShuffled(rng) that returns a fresh ordering vector: start with a copy of order1, then for each tier_group apply Fisher-Yates shuffle to the slice of order1 at that group's positions using rng; pieces stay within their maxArea tier so the large-first principle is preserved while ties are broken differently each call. In the W loop, replace the current order1-then-order2 fallback with this extended chain: try order1; if fail try order2; for trial r in 0..7 generate shuffled = makeShuffled(rng) and try shuffled; if all ten fail increment W. The first successful tryPack copies its temp arrays (tX,tY,tR,tF) into outX/outY/outR/outF and breaks. Reuse a single col_bits allocation re-zeroed at the start of each tryPack call. The K-lookahead step loop from iter-6 is removed; tryPack returns to the iter-3 form that walks the given order linearly placing one piece at each step using findBest. Output unchanged: line one is W W, then n lines of X Y R F in original input order.
rationale: Within-maxArea shuffling preserves the large-first principle but lets BL explore many different sub-orderings at each W, giving 10 chances at the minimum feasible W instead of 2 and exposing tighter packings that the two fixed orderings happen to miss; this opens a new direction since pure scoring-tweak iters 4 and 5 and the lookahead iter 6 all failed to improve on iter 3.

approach: Burke best-fit lowest-skyline with bounded candidate pool
details: Revert to c795078 (iter 3 baseline). Keep all iter-3 structures: 8 orientations per piece (min_tx, min_ty, w, h, cells, cols, min_dy, max_dy, pattern_dx); per-column bitmap col_bits; bitmap shift-OR collision; contact count C; per-piece recovery X=x0-min_tx, Y=y0-min_ty, R=orientation modulo 4, F=orientation divided by 4. Replace the fixed-order BL placement loop with a Burke-style best-fit lowest-skyline placement loop. Add a precomputed priorityOrder (sort piece indices by maxArea desc, then ks desc) computed once in main. Add per-piece min_w_orient = min over 8 orientations of o.w and min_h_orient = min over 8 orientations of o.h. Inside tryPack: reset col_bits to zeros; add skyline of length W initialized to zeros; add placed boolean array of length n initialized to false; let remaining = n. Outer step loop while remaining greater than 0. Step a: find min_h = min of skyline; find leftmost lo where skyline[lo] equals min_h; extend hi past lo to the smallest index where skyline[hi] does not equal min_h (hi = W if the gap reaches the right edge); compute w_gap = hi - lo; h_left = (lo equals 0) then INT_MAX else skyline[lo-1]; h_right = (hi equals W) then INT_MAX else skyline[hi]. Step b: build a candidate pool of up to K = 24 unplaced piece indices by walking priorityOrder linearly, skipping placed entries, and including pi only if min_w_orient[pi] is at most w_gap and min_h + min_h_orient[pi] is at most W; stop after K accepted entries. Step c: for each candidate pi in the pool, for each orientation oi where o.w is at most w_gap and min_h + o.h is at most W, for x0 in [lo, hi - o.w]: set y0 = min_h (the gap floor is uniformly min_h across [lo, hi) by construction so the bitmap drop reduces to y0 = min_h and the bitmap collision check is unnecessary). Score waste = (x0 - lo) + (hi - x0 - o.w); top = y0 + o.h; if waste is greater than bestWaste then skip the candidate immediately without computing C (early prune). Compute contact count C exactly as in iter 3 (4-neighbor count of cells that are out of bounds in [0,W)x[0,W) or whose bit is set in col_bits at the neighbor column, excluding piece-own cells via a small pmask of o.w by o.h). Track the best (pi, oi, x0, y0) across all candidates using lex tuple (waste ascending, C descending, top ascending, x0 ascending). Step d: if a best was found, place it by setting bits in col_bits at (x0+cx, y0+cy) for each cell c of o.cells; set placed[pi] = true; decrement remaining; for each column gx in [x0, x0+o.w) update skyline[gx] = max(skyline[gx], y0 + o.max_dy[gx - x0] + 1); record tF[pi] = oi divided by 4, tR[pi] = oi modulo 4, tX[pi] = x0 - o.min_tx, tY[pi] = y0 - o.min_ty. Step e: if no best was found in this step, compute new_h = min(h_left, h_right); if new_h equals INT_MAX or new_h is at least W return false from tryPack; otherwise raise the gap by writing skyline[c] = new_h for c in [lo, hi) and continue the outer loop. Drop order2, drop the multi-shuffled fallback, drop the iter-6 K-lookahead logic; the Burke loop is the sole packer per W. Main W loop: start W = ceil(sqrt(T)); on each iteration allocate col_bits and temporary tX tY tR tF arrays, call tryPack once; on success copy temporaries to outX outY outR outF and break; on failure free temporaries, increment W, and retry. Output unchanged: first line is W W; then n lines of X Y R F in original input order. Edge note: when w_gap equals W (initial state) the candidate pool naturally includes the largest pieces first via priorityOrder; when w_gap shrinks during play the early-prune on waste plus the min_w_orient filter keep the inner search fast.
rationale: Burke best-fit lowest-skyline is a fundamentally different paradigm from fixed-order BL because piece selection is driven by the geometry of the current lowest skyline gap rather than a pre-sorted iteration order so awkward concave pockets that fixed-order BL misses get filled by whichever unplaced piece best matches the gap width; this opens a new direction since iters 4 through 7 (scoring tweaks, K-lookahead, shuffled multi-start) all flattened around the iter-3 score of 75.58.

approach: BL with diverse deterministic ordering chain
details: Revert to c795078 (iter-3 baseline). Keep every iter-3 structure: 8 orientations per piece (min_tx, min_ty, w, h, cells, cols, min_dy, max_dy, pattern_dx); true-BL via per-column bitmap col_bits with shift-OR aggregation into total_blocked and ctzll lowest-zero search; contact-count C; lex tuple (y0+h ascending, C descending, y0 ascending, x0 ascending); per-piece recovery X=x0-min_tx, Y=y0-min_ty, R=orientation modulo 4, F=orientation divided by 4. The single change is at the ordering chain inside main. Compute these five deterministic orderings up front from the 8 orientation summaries per piece: order1 by maxArea desc then k desc (existing); order2 by maxDim desc then k desc then maxArea desc (existing); order3 (new) by perimeter desc then maxArea desc then k desc where perimeter equals 2 times (maxOrientW plus maxOrientH) and maxOrientW, maxOrientH are the max over 8 orientations of o.w and o.h; order4 (new) by k_i desc then maxArea desc then maxDim desc; order5 (new) by minBboxArea desc then maxArea desc then k desc where minBboxArea is the min over 8 orientations of o.w times o.h (rewards pieces whose smallest-footprint orientation is still large). In the W loop starting at W = ceil(sqrt(T)), at each W try order1; on failure reset col_bits and the temp tX, tY, tR, tF arrays to zero and try order2; on failure reset and try order3; on failure reset and try order4; on failure reset and try order5; if all five fail, increment W and continue. The first ordering that returns true from tryPack copies its temp arrays into outX, outY, outR, outF and the W loop breaks. Reuse a single col_bits allocation and one set of temp arrays across trials (re-zero them at the start of every tryPack call). Do not introduce any randomness, shuffles, lookahead, gap_sum, floor_match, or skyline-evenness logic; the per-piece inner BL engine (orientation loop, bitmap shift-OR, ctzll lowest-zero, contact-count scoring, lex tuple selection, per-piece recovery) is byte-for-byte identical to iter-3. Output unchanged: line one W W, then n lines of X Y R F in original input order.
rationale: The iter-3 BL engine has matured around 75.5 with two orderings and pure scoring tweaks (iters 4 and 5) have not helped; widening only the ordering chain with five meaningfully distinct deterministic criteria is the cheapest way to expose a smaller feasible W on tests where order1 and order2 both deadlock, and unlike iter-7 deterministic orderings avoid the cost and instability of eight random shuffles per W.

approach: BL with single-step chronological backtracking on placement failure
details: Revert to c795078 (iter-3 baseline). Keep every iter-3 structure intact: 8 orientations per piece (min_tx, min_ty, w, h, cells, cols, min_dy, max_dy, pattern_dx); true-BL via per-column bitmap col_bits with shift-OR aggregation into total_blocked and ctzll lowest-zero search bounded by y0 at most W minus o.h; contact-count C; lex tuple (y0+h ascending, C descending, y0 ascending, x0 ascending); per-piece recovery X = x0 minus o.min_tx, Y = y0 minus o.min_ty, R = orientation modulo 4, F = orientation divided by 4; order1 by maxArea desc then k desc; order2 by maxDim desc then k desc then maxArea desc; fallback chain of try order1, then order2, then W increment. The single change is inside tryPack. Refactor findBest into findTopK that returns the top up to K = 4 valid placements as a vector of records (oi, x0, y0, s1=y0+h, C) sorted ascending by the iter-3 lex tuple (y0+h asc then C desc then y0 asc then x0 asc); if fewer than K valid placements exist, return what exists; empty vector means no placement at all. In tryPack add per-step vectors lastList of length n where lastList[step] holds the top-K record list for the piece chosen at that step, and an integer array choice of length n holding the chosen index into lastList[step] (initialized to 0 when a step first becomes active). Walk step from 0 upward. At each step let pi = order[step]; call findTopK on pi against the current col_bits and store the result into lastList[step] with choice[step] = 0; if lastList[step] is empty enter backtrack; otherwise apply choice 0 by iterating the cells of orients[pi][lastList[step][0].oi] and setting bit (y at row) in col_bits at column lastList[step][0].x0 + cx (concretely col_bits[gx][gy shifted right by 6] OR-equals 1ULL shifted left by (gy AND 63)), record tF[pi], tR[pi], tX[pi], tY[pi] for the applied record, and advance step by 1. Backtrack subroutine: increment a global bt_count; if bt_count exceeds MAX_BT = 4 times n return false; if step equals 0 return false; otherwise prevStep = step minus 1; clear the cells of lastList[prevStep][choice[prevStep]] from col_bits (iterate the orientation cells and AND-equals NOT mask at the same bit positions); choice[prevStep] = choice[prevStep] + 1; if choice[prevStep] is less than the size of lastList[prevStep] then apply the new choice (write its cells into col_bits, refresh tF, tR, tX, tY for order[prevStep] from that new record), set step = prevStep + 1, return to the main step loop; if choice[prevStep] equals the size of lastList[prevStep] then recurse into Backtrack again with step = prevStep. If step ever reaches n return true. Output format unchanged: line one W W, then n lines X Y R F in original input order. Edge note: lastList and choice are sized to n at tryPack entry and re-zeroed alongside col_bits; bt_count resets to 0 at each tryPack entry; the order2 fallback still applies if backtracking fully fails for order1 at this W.
rationale: Bounded chronological backtracking lets BL recover from rare placement dead-ends where the greedy top-1 choice for an earlier piece walls off a later piece, while iters 4 to 9 only varied scoring or ordering and so could never undo a prior bad choice; this opens a structurally new direction at modest cost since most steps still take the top-1 choice and never rewind.

details: Revert to c795078 (iter-3 baseline). Keep every iter-3 structure intact: 8 orientations per piece (min_tx, min_ty, w, h, cells, cols, min_dy, max_dy, pattern_dx); true-BL via per-column bitmap col_bits with shift-OR aggregation into total_blocked and ctzll lowest-zero search bounded by y0 at most W minus o.h; contact-count C; lex tuple (y0+h ascending, C descending, y0 ascending, x0 ascending); per-piece recovery X = x0 minus o.min_tx, Y = y0 minus o.min_ty, R = orientation modulo 4, F = orientation divided by 4; order1 by maxArea desc then k desc; order2 by maxDim desc then k desc then maxArea desc; outer fallback chain of try order1, then order2, then W increment. The single change is inside tryPack: replace the linear walk through order with a dynamic most-constrained-first selector. At tryPack entry add a placed boolean array of length n initialized to false, an integer scanFront initialized to 0, and an integer remaining initialized to n; zero col_bits as usual. Outer step loop while remaining is greater than 0. Step a (candidate pool): advance scanFront past any leading already-placed entries in order; then scan order from scanFront forward collecting up to K = 6 unplaced piece indices into a vector cands; if cands is empty return true. Step b (cheap freedom count): for each pi in cands compute freedom[pi] by iterating orientations oi from 0 to 7 (skip any orientation with o.w greater than W or o.h greater than W) and for each x0 from 0 to W minus o.w running the iter-3 bitmap shift-OR aggregation into total_blocked plus ctzll lowest-zero search; if a valid y0 at most W minus o.h is found increment freedom[pi]; stop incrementing once freedom[pi] reaches FREEDOM_CAP = 8 (early-exit both the x0 loop and the orientation loop to keep cost flat). Do NOT compute contact-count C in step b; this pass is for counting only. If after the full scan freedom[pi] equals 0 record pi as infeasible. Step c (selection): if any cand is infeasible return false (this W is dead for this ordering); otherwise pick the cand with smallest freedom[pi]; tiebreak by earliest position in order (which by construction is largest maxArea then largest k). Call the chosen index pi-star. Step d (placement): run iter-3 findBest on pi-star against current col_bits (this is the full iter-3 inner search including contact-count C and the full lex tuple selection) to get the best record (oi, x0, y0); apply it by setting bit (y0 plus c.second) in word ((y0 plus c.second) divided by 64) of col_bits[x0 plus c.first] for each cell c of orients[pi-star][oi].cells; set placed[pi-star] true; decrement remaining; record tF[pi-star] = oi divided by 4, tR[pi-star] = oi modulo 4, tX[pi-star] = x0 minus o.min_tx, tY[pi-star] = y0 minus o.min_ty. Continue to next step. Reuse a single col_bits allocation re-zeroed at tryPack entry. Output format unchanged: line one is W W; subsequent n lines are X Y R F in original input order. Edge note: when the grid is mostly empty every candidate hits FREEDOM_CAP and the tiebreak selects the order1 head, so early packing matches iter-3 exactly; fail-first only takes effect when at least one candidate has freedom strictly below the cap, which is the late-pack regime where iter-3 dead-ends and forces W increment.
rationale: Most-constrained-variable (fail-first) is the standard CSP heuristic for tight packings; it preempts the late-step dead-end where iter-3 fixed-order BL fails because a specific endangered piece runs out of valid placements while easier pieces sit ahead of it in order, and it opens a structurally new direction since iter 6 selected the BEST-fitting candidate (opposite criterion), iters 4 and 5 only tweaked scoring, iters 7 and 9 only varied static orderings, iter 8 used a non-BL Burke selector, and iter 10 added backtracking rather than dynamic piece selection.

approach: BL with future-feasibility tiebreak on placement candidates
details: Revert to c795078 (iter-3 baseline). Keep every iter-3 structure intact: 8 orientations per piece (min_tx, min_ty, w, h, cells, cols, min_dy, max_dy, pattern_dx); true-BL via per-column bitmap col_bits with shift-OR aggregation into total_blocked and ctzll lowest-zero search bounded by y0 at most W minus o.h; contact-count C; per-piece recovery X = x0 minus o.min_tx, Y = y0 minus o.min_ty, R = orientation modulo 4, F = orientation divided by 4; order1 by maxArea desc then k desc; order2 by maxDim desc then k desc then maxArea desc; outer fallback chain of try order1, then order2, then W increment. The single change is inside findBest, applied identically when called from either order1 or order2 tryPack. Refactor findBest to take the current order vector, the current step index, and the placed-array, in addition to col_bits and the piece index pi. Stage 1: enumerate all valid candidates exactly as iter-3 does (for each orientation oi from 0 to 7 with o.w at most W and o.h at most W, for each x0 from 0 to W minus o.w, run the shift-OR aggregation across all dx in o.cols and all dy in pattern_dx[dx] into total_blocked, OR in the upper-tail mask for indices at least W minus o.h plus 1, find the lowest 0-bit y0 via word-wise ctzll on the bitwise NOT, accept if y0 is at most W minus o.h). For each accepted candidate compute the contact count C as in iter-3 (iterate cells, examine 4 neighbors, count out-of-bounds or set-bit-in-col_bits neighbors excluding piece-own cells via the pmask). Store each accepted candidate as a struct (oi, x0, y0, s1 equal to y0 plus o.h, C). If no candidate accepted return false. Stage 2: find best_s1 equal to the minimum s1 across all candidates. Build tie_set as the candidates with s1 equal to best_s1. If tie_set size is 1 apply that candidate and return true. Stage 3 (only if tie_set size is greater than 1): pre-sort tie_set by (C descending, y0 ascending, x0 ascending) and truncate to the first 6 entries to bound compute. For each remaining record compute future_block as follows. Tentatively set the bits for this record cells in col_bits (for each cell c in orients[pi][record.oi].cells set bit (record.y0 plus c.second) of col_bits[record.x0 plus c.first] at word index shifted right by 6 and bit index AND 63). Let L = 3. For step_next in step+1 to min(step+L, n-1), let pi_next = order[step_next]; if placed[pi_next] is true skip; otherwise run a feasibility-only scan over orientations oi_n from 0 to 7 (skip o.w greater than W or o.h greater than W) and for each oi_n iterate x0_n from 0 to W minus o.w; for each (oi_n, x0_n) build a fresh total_blocked exactly as in stage 1 (shift-OR across o.cols and pattern_dx[dx], OR in the upper-tail mask, find lowest 0-bit y0_n via word-wise ctzll); if any (oi_n, x0_n) yields y0_n at most W minus o.h mark pi_next feasible and break out of both the x0_n and oi_n loops for this pi_next; if no orientation and no x0_n yields any valid y0_n increment future_block by 1. After checking all next pieces clear the tentative bits from col_bits (for each cell c in the record AND-equal NOT mask). Stage 4: among the truncated tie_set pick the record with smallest (future_block ascending, then C descending, then y0 ascending, then x0 ascending). Apply that record: set bits in col_bits, set placed[pi] true, record tF[pi] = record.oi divided by 4, tR[pi] = record.oi modulo 4, tX[pi] = record.x0 minus o.min_tx, tY[pi] = record.y0 minus o.min_ty. tryPack stays a linear walk over order; pass step and the order vector into findBest. Reuse a single col_bits allocation re-zeroed at the start of each tryPack call. Edge cases: when step + L is at least n the next-piece loop terminates naturally; placed-pieces are skipped without being counted; an empty tie_set is impossible because stage 2 always finds at least one record; when tie_set is reduced to size 1 after truncation skip stage 3 entirely. Output format unchanged: line one W W, then n lines X Y R F in original input order.
rationale: Addresses greedy myopia at the placement-choice level for the first time without disturbing piece ordering: among placements tied at the lowest top-edge, prefer ones that do not strand upcoming large pieces with zero valid positions, attacking the late-pack dead-end that forces iter-3 to bump W while preserving the natural large-first BL flow that iters 6, 7, 9, 10, 11 broke by changing piece-selection or ordering.

approach: BL with bounded ejection-chain on placement failure
details: Revert to c795078 (iter-3 baseline). Keep every iter-3 structure intact: 8 orientations per piece (min_tx, min_ty, w, h, cells, cols, min_dy, max_dy, pattern_dx); true-BL via per-column bitmap col_bits with shift-OR aggregation into total_blocked and ctzll lowest-zero search bounded by y0 at most W minus o.h; contact-count C; lex tuple (y0+h ascending, C descending, y0 ascending, x0 ascending); per-piece recovery X = x0 minus o.min_tx, Y = y0 minus o.min_ty, R = orientation modulo 4, F = orientation divided by 4; order1 by maxArea desc then k desc; order2 by maxDim desc then k desc then maxArea desc; outer fallback chain of try order1, then order2, then W increment. The single change is inside tryPack and ONLY activates when iter-3 findBest returns no valid placement for the current piece P. Track per-piece placement_map[pi] = (oi, x0, y0) for each successfully placed piece, and a global integer eject_budget initialized to 4 times n at tryPack entry (with col_bits and placement_map both reset to empty at tryPack entry). Add a placement_history vector that appends pi at the end whenever pi is placed and pops the last entry whenever pi is removed. Maintain a placed boolean array of length n initialized to false. In tryPack, walk step from 0 to n-1 over the given order vector. At each step let pi = order[step]; call iter-3 findBest for pi against current col_bits. If findBest succeeds with (oi_P, x0_P, y0_P), apply it (set bits for cells of orients[pi][oi_P] at (x0_P + c.first, y0_P + c.second) into col_bits[gx] word index (gy shifted right by 6) bit (gy AND 63), set placed[pi] = true, set placement_map[pi] = (oi_P, x0_P, y0_P), append pi to placement_history, write tF tR tX tY for pi), and continue. If findBest fails for pi enter ejection-chain. Ejection-chain procedure: scan placement_history from latest entry backward, collecting up to K_eject = 12 placed-piece candidates pi_prime; for each candidate clear its cells from col_bits (iterate cells of orients[pi_prime][placement_map[pi_prime].oi] and AND-equal NOT mask at the same column word and bit), then call iter-3 findBest for pi against the modified col_bits; if findBest returns a valid record (oi_P, x0_P, y0_P), record the candidate with cost = y0_P + orients[pi][oi_P].h and restore pi_prime cells (re-write the bits); if findBest still fails, restore pi_prime cells and continue. After collecting all candidate records sort them by cost ascending. For each candidate (pi_prime, oi_P, x0_P, y0_P) in that sorted list, attempt the two-piece reshuffle: clear pi_prime cells from col_bits; tentatively set pi cells at (oi_P, x0_P, y0_P) into col_bits; call iter-3 findBest for pi_prime against the new col_bits; if findBest returns valid (oi_Pp_new, x0_Pp_new, y0_Pp_new) for pi_prime, commit the reshuffle by writing pi_prime cells at the new position into col_bits, updating placement_map[pi_prime] = (oi_Pp_new, x0_Pp_new, y0_Pp_new), updating tF tR tX tY for pi_prime, setting placed[pi] = true, setting placement_map[pi] = (oi_P, x0_P, y0_P), appending pi to placement_history at the end, writing tF tR tX tY for pi, decrementing eject_budget by 1, then breaking out of the candidate loop and advancing to step+1 in the main walk. If findBest for pi_prime fails, clear pi cells and restore pi_prime cells to its old position then continue to the next candidate. If all K_eject candidates fail to yield a two-piece reshuffle, or if eject_budget reaches 0 before a successful reshuffle, return false from tryPack so the outer W loop falls back to order2 then to W increment. Reuse a single col_bits allocation re-zeroed at tryPack entry; placement_map can be a fixed array of length n, placement_history a vector capped at n. Edge note: when ejection succeeds the pi_prime moves later in placement_history than its original position so subsequent backtracking still finds it; the K_eject cap and eject_budget cap together bound total ejection work to at most 4 times n outer attempts. Output format unchanged: line one W W; subsequent n lines X Y R F in original input order.
rationale: Ejection-chain (kick-move) attacks the boundary case where iter-3 fails at a smaller W because one earlier piece walls off a critical position for a later piece; unlike iter-10 which retried the SAME chronological piece with top-K alternative placements (often barely different), this lifts a DIFFERENT piece chosen by which lift unblocks the failed piece, opening a structurally new recovery mode that targets W minus 1 where iter-3 would otherwise bump to W.

details: Keep every iter-13 structure intact: 8 orientations per piece (min_tx, min_ty, w, h, cells, cols, min_dy, max_dy, pattern_dx); true-BL via per-column bitmap col_bits with shift-OR aggregation into total_blocked and ctzll lowest-zero search bounded by y0 at most W minus o.h; contact-count C; iter-3 lex tuple (y0+h ascending, C descending, y0 ascending, x0 ascending) in findBest; per-piece recovery X = x0 minus o.min_tx, Y = y0 minus o.min_ty, R = orientation modulo 4, F = orientation divided by 4; order1 by maxArea desc then k desc; order2 by maxDim desc then k desc then maxArea desc; outer fallback chain of try order1, then order2, then W increment; placement_map[pi] storing (oi, x0, y0) for placed pieces; placement_history vector of placed pi indices; placed boolean array; eject_budget integer initialized at tryPack entry. The single change is to generalize iter-13's single-step ejection into a depth-2 recursive ejection chain. Replace the inline ejection block inside tryPack with a recursive helper place_with_ejection(pi, depth) that returns true on success and false on failure. Algorithm of place_with_ejection(pi, depth): step 1 call iter-3 findBest for pi against current col_bits; if it returns a valid (oi_P, x0_P, y0_P), set bits in col_bits for cells of orients[pi][oi_P] at (x0_P + c.first, y0_P + c.second) using col_bits[gx][gy shifted right by 6] OR equal 1ULL shifted left by (gy AND 63), set placed[pi] true, set placement_map[pi] equal to (oi_P, x0_P, y0_P), append pi to placement_history, record tF[pi] equal to oi_P divided by 4, tR[pi] equal to oi_P modulo 4, tX[pi] equal to x0_P minus o.min_tx, tY[pi] equal to y0_P minus o.min_ty, and return true. Step 2 if findBest failed and depth is at least MAX_DEPTH (set MAX_DEPTH equal to 2) return false. Step 3 if eject_budget is at most 0 return false; otherwise decrement eject_budget by 1. Step 4 set K_eject equal to 12 when depth equals 0 and equal to 8 when depth equals 1. Step 5 scan placement_history from the last entry backward up to K_eject entries; for each candidate pi_prime clear pi_prime cells from col_bits by iterating cells of orients[pi_prime][placement_map[pi_prime].oi] and AND-equal NOT mask at the same word and bit; call iter-3 findBest for pi against the modified col_bits; if findBest returns a valid record (oi_P, x0_P, y0_P) store the candidate as a struct with fields pi_prime, oi_P, x0_P, y0_P, cost equal to y0_P plus orients[pi][oi_P].h, hist_idx equal to the history index; restore pi_prime cells back into col_bits regardless. Step 6 sort the collected candidates by cost ascending. Step 7 for each candidate (pi_prime, oi_P, x0_P, y0_P, cost, hist_idx) in sorted order: a) remove pi_prime from placement_history by erasing entry at hist_idx (use std erase); set placed[pi_prime] false; clear pi_prime cells from col_bits; clear placement_map[pi_prime]; b) set bits in col_bits for pi cells at (x0_P + c.first, y0_P + c.second); set placed[pi] true; set placement_map[pi] equal to (oi_P, x0_P, y0_P); append pi to placement_history; record tF[pi], tR[pi], tX[pi], tY[pi]; c) recursively call place_with_ejection(pi_prime, depth plus 1); d) if the recursive call returns true commit by returning true (pi and pi_prime are now both placed in col_bits and placement_history); e) if the recursive call returns false roll back: clear pi cells from col_bits, set placed[pi] false, remove pi from placement_history (it was appended last so pop_back), clear placement_map[pi]; restore pi_prime to its prior position by setting bits in col_bits for pi_prime cells at the saved old (oi, x0, y0), set placed[pi_prime] true, set placement_map[pi_prime] back to the saved old record, re-insert pi_prime into placement_history at hist_idx (use std insert); continue to next candidate. Step 8 if all candidates exhausted return false. In tryPack the main step loop becomes a simple call place_with_ejection(order[step], 0) and on false return false to the outer W fallback. Initialize eject_budget equal to 8 times n at tryPack entry (doubled vs iter-13 to absorb the deeper search); reset placement_history empty; reset placed array to false; reset placement_map; zero col_bits. Edge note: when MAX_DEPTH equals 1 the recursive call at depth 1 immediately hits the depth gate and returns false unless its findBest succeeds outright, so this exactly reproduces iter-13 behavior under the new code path; with MAX_DEPTH equal to 2 the depth-1 recursive call performs one further ejection layer using K_eject equal to 8, allowing pi_prime to displace some pi_dp whose move makes room for pi_prime. Output format unchanged: line one W W, then n lines X Y R F in original input order.
rationale: Recursive depth-2 ejection extends the iter-13 chain so that when the displaced pi_prime cannot find a direct home it gets a second chance to displace another piece, recovering W minus 1 placements that iter-13 abandons after one lift; this deepens the maturing iter-13 direction which just produced a new best of 76.20 over iter-3 at 75.58.
